data.name: Illyssa
data.gender_notes: Illyssa is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Illyssa was the goddess of nature and fertility. Her name is derived from the Greek word 'ilysso', which means ‘to go’. In Christianity, the name Illyssa may be used as a variant of Helen or Elissa, both of which have biblical origins and significant meanings. The name Illyssa carries the meaning “Goddess of nature and fertility” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Illyssa usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of nature and fertility and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Illyssa belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of nature and fertility.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Illyssa total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_greek.name: Ιλλύσσα
in_greek.long_meaning: Τὸ ὄνομα Ιλλύσσα προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὸ ἑλληνικὸ 'Ἰλλυσος', ποῦ σημαίνει 'ἀνεβασμένο' ἤ 'Θεός εἰς τὴν σωτηρίαν μου'. Τὸ ὄνομα αὐτὸ χρησιμοποιεῖται εὐρέως στὴν παράδοση τῆς Χριστιανικῆς Οἰκουμενικῆς.

in_latin.name: Illyssa

historical_references.reference: Illyssa, according to some legends, was a Cretan princess who was the lover of the god Dionysus. She was transformed into a snake by Hera, jealous of her relationship with the god. This myth is believed to date back to ancient Greek times, around 500 BCE.

Illyssa is also mentioned in Christian folklore as a virgin martyr who lived during the late Roman Empire. She is said to have been martyred during the Diocletian Persecution around 304 CE, along with her mother and two sisters. Her relics are believed to be located in the church of San Leonardo in Selvite, Italy.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Illyssa is a beautiful and unique name, derived from the ancient Greek goddess Illysia. In modern times, this name has gained popularity in various contexts, particularly in the worlds of fantasy role-playing games, mythological character names, and as a baby name. In the realm of fantasy RPG games, Illyssa is a name often given to powerful and enchanting female characters, such as sorceresses, druids, or demigoddesses. In mythology, Illyssa is a name referenced in works of literature and storytelling, often representing a goddess of love, beauty, and nature. As a baby name, Illyssa has seen an increase in usage due to its exotic and elegant sound, as well as its connection to the rich history and mythology of ancient Greece.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Sarah Illyssa in Athens, Greece credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Illyssa, which means "Goddess of nature and fertility". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
